# Overview

MEWOC implements Bayesian dose finding for single-agent phase I trials with
escalation with overdose control (EWOC). Clinicians give prior probabilities that
the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) lies below the minimum dose (`p0`) or above the
maximum dose (`p1`); MEWOC calibrates the prior to these probabilities, simulates
the operating characteristics of the design, and supports the conduct of the
trial cohort by cohort. The same functions run the interactive app, started with
`run_mewoc_app()`.

The examples below use small MCMC settings, few simulated trials and one worker
so that the vignette builds quickly. For a real design use the app defaults
(burn-in 1000, 1500 MCMC samples) and many more trials (for example 1000 or more).

```{r setup}
library(MEWOC)
```

# 1. Calibrate the prior

```{r prior}
prior <- run_mewoc_grid_search(theta = 0.33, p0 = 0.1, p1 = 0.2, condition = 2,
                               seed = 1, n_prior = 6000, bobyqa_starts = 1)
prior[, c("a0", "b0", "a1", "b1", "matched_p0", "matched_p1")]
```

The matched probabilities should be close to the targets `p0 = 0.1` and
`p1 = 0.2`. Calibration, plotting and posterior fitting all use a beta prior
for the maximum-dose DLT probability truncated to `[0.001, 0.999]`.
Recalibrate prior settings generated by earlier versions that calibrated without
this truncation. The prior probability of a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) at each dose:

```{r prior-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
build_prior_plot(prior, num_doses = 4, seed_value = 1,
                 dose_labels = c("10 mg", "20 mg", "30 mg", "40 mg"))
```

# 2. Simulate a design with discrete doses

```{r discrete}
discrete_inputs <- list(
  M = 4, NN = 12, cohort = 3, dose_type = "Discrete",
  num_doses = 4, startdose = 1, doseprobs = c(0.05, 0.15, 0.33, 0.50),
  actual_dose_levels = c(10, 20, 30, 40), dose_unit = "mg",
  theta = 0.33, deltastop = 0.85, lower_f_bound = 0.25, increment = 0.05,
  alpha_increment_cutoff = 0.33, burn = 200, mm = 300, seed = 988,
  trial_mode = "Standard EWOC", max_accel_dose_level = NA,
  stopping_rule_selected = FALSE, num_patients_restrict = NA)
discrete_sims <- run_trial_simulations_background(discrete_inputs, prior, ncores = 1)
discrete_summary <- summarize_trial_simulation_results(discrete_sims, discrete_inputs)
discrete_summary$combined_table
discrete_summary$stopping_summary_table
```

One simulated trial can also be run directly; `incr` is the standardized
distance between adjacent levels (1/3 for four equally spaced levels). The API
uses one chain (`chains = 1`). The posterior MTD alpha-quantile is rounded to the
nearest discrete level, subject to dose limits and the no-skipping rule; the
rounded dose can have a posterior overdose probability above alpha. When the
toxicity rule allows an alpha increase, it is capped at exactly 0.5, including
when an increment would cross 0.5:

```{r one-trial}
set.seed(2)
one_trial <- run_single_trial_simulation(
  trial_id = 1, doselevels = seq(0, 1, length.out = 4),
  doseprobs = c(0.05, 0.15, 0.33, 0.50), startdose = 1, cohort = 3, NN = 12,
  alpha = seq(0.25, 0.5, by = 0.05), theta = 0.33, burn = 200, mm = 300,
  chains = 1, opt1 = prior, stopping_rule_selected = FALSE,
  num_patients_restrict = NA, incr = 1 / 3)
data.frame(patient = seq_along(one_trial$dose), dose_level = one_trial$dose * 3 + 1,
           dlt = one_trial$dlt)
```

# 3. Simulate a design with a continuous dose range

The true dose-toxicity curve is given by the true MTD and the true DLT
probability at the minimum dose.

```{r continuous}
continuous_inputs <- list(
  M = 2, NN = 9, cohort = 3, dose_type = "Continuous",
  min_dose = 10, max_dose = 50, dose_unit = "mg", max_dose_increment = 10,
  true_mtd = 30, true_p_min = 0.1,
  theta = 0.33, deltastop = 0.85, lower_f_bound = 0.25, increment = 0.05,
  alpha_increment_cutoff = 0.33, burn = 200, mm = 300, seed = 988,
  trial_mode = "Standard EWOC", max_accel_dose_level = NA,
  stopping_rule_selected = FALSE, num_patients_restrict = NA,
  efficiency_stop_tolerance = NA)
continuous_sims <- run_trial_simulations_background(continuous_inputs, prior, ncores = 1)
sapply(continuous_sims$results, function(trial) trial$vmtd)
continuous_summary <- summarize_trial_simulation_results(continuous_sims, continuous_inputs)
continuous_summary$combined_table
```

# 4. Trial Conduct

Before the trial, write the Trial Conduct workbook with the design settings and
an empty patient sheet:

```{r workbook}
design_table <- rbind(
  build_conduct_design_table(
    p0 = 0.1, p1 = 0.2, a0 = prior$a0, b0 = prior$b0, a1 = prior$a1, b1 = prior$b1,
    num_doses = 4, startdose = 1, theta = 0.33, deltastop = 0.85,
    lower_f_bound = 0.25, increment = 0.05, trial_mode = "Standard EWOC",
    max_accel_dose_level = NA, seed = 988, burn = 1000, mm = 1500),
  conduct_trial_rule_rows(cohort_size = 3, total_sample_size = 30))
workbook <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
write_conduct_workbook(workbook, design_table, build_conduct_patient_template())
file.exists(workbook)
```

During the trial, evaluate the data entered so far to get the dose for the next
cohort:

```{r conduct}
design <- list(dose_type = "Discrete", dose_unit = "mg", num_doses = 4, startdose = 1,
               actual_dose_levels = c(10, 20, 30, 40), dose_units = rep("mg", 4),
               doselevels = seq(0, 1, length.out = 4),
               min_dose = NA, max_dose = NA, max_dose_increment = NA)
settings <- list(theta = 0.33, deltastop = 0.85, lower_alpha = 0.25, increment = 0.05,
                 alpha_increment_cutoff = 0.33, burn = 200, mm = 300, seed = 7,
                 trial_mode = "Standard EWOC", max_accel_dose_level = NA,
                 cohort_size = 3, total_sample_size = 30, efficiency_rule = FALSE,
                 num_patients_restrict = NA, efficiency_width = NA)
rows <- data.frame(Cohort = rep(c("1", "2"), each = 3), Patient = as.character(1:6),
                   Administered_Dose = c(10, 10, 10, 20, 20, 20),
                   DLT = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 0L), Is_Unevaluable = FALSE,
                   Uploaded_Recommended_Dose = NA, Uploaded_Alpha_Used = NA)
evaluation <- conduct_evaluate_trial(rows, design, settings, prior)
evaluation$next_recommendation$dose
evaluation$alpha_for_next
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(workbook)
```

# References

Babb J, Rogatko A, Zacks S (1998). Cancer phase I clinical trials: efficient dose
escalation with overdose control. *Statistics in Medicine*, 17(10), 1103-1120.

Tighiouart M, Rogatko A (2010). Dose finding with escalation with overdose control
(EWOC) in cancer clinical trials. *Statistical Science*, 25(2), 217-226.

Wheeler GM, Sweeting MJ, Mander AP (2017). Toxicity-dependent feasibility bounds
for the escalation with overdose control approach in phase I cancer trials.
*Statistics in Medicine*, 36(16), 2499-2513.
